subject: Renewal discussion: 16 GPU reserved pool transition & throughput SLOs
messages:
From: Ivy Chen <ivy@novusai.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-12T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal planning — wanting to double reserved capacity

Hey Marcus,

We’re kicking off our renewal planning for Q3 and want to explore moving our Dedicated pool from 8→16 GPUs at renewal. Usage has jumped (inference throughput up ~2.1x) and our ops team is asking for a short list of guarantees and operational controls before we commit.

Top asks from Novus ops:
- A throughput SLO per GPU (or per-pool) for 95th percentile latency for our 1.2k token median requests
- An activation timeline — how quickly extra GPUs can be live after signature
- Fallback policy: what happens if capacity pressure occurs during our ramp (model-level fallback or burst pool?)
- Billing/proration on mid-cycle increases and invoicing cadence

Can you send a proposed amendment and a high-level activation playbook so we can review with procurement and SRE? We’re targeting a firm decision by the end of next week.

Thanks —
Ivy Chen
VP of Platform, NovusAI

--
NovusAI | Platform & Data
ops@novusai.com
From: marcus_lin@redwood.com <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Ivy Chen <ivy@novusai.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-12T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — wanting to double reserved capacity

Ivy — thanks for the clear list. We can support a 8→16 reserved pool transition at renewal. Attaching a draft amendment that captures the commercial change and proposed SLOs. High level answers: 

- Throughput/latency SLO: we can commit to 95th percentile generation latency <= 250ms for sequences up to 1.5k tokens on your pinned model profile under our Dedicated tier, measured at the per-route level in Redwood Console. We’ll include a credit schedule for SLO misses.

- Activation timeline: standard activation is 14 business days after countersignature for a full 16-GPU pool from Dedicated capacity (we can prioritize your activation window earlier as a one-time ramp for an additional mobilization fee; see amendment).

- Fallback policy: we recommend an ordered fallback: 1) auto-route to compatible quantized variant within Dedicated capacity, 2) short-term burst to shared-hosted capacity with soft throttles, 3) automatic throttling by route if sustained pressure. We’ll document guardrails (max-burst minutes/day) so SRE can plan.

- Billing: monthly invoiced commit; mid-cycle increases are prorated daily. We’ll include an invoice timing option (Net30 or Net45) on the amendment.

Laura — dropping you in to send the redline and final amendment. Grace — can you draft the activation checklist and an ops runbook itemizing the fallback behavior and KV cache migration notes?

Marcus Lin
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ivy Chen <ivy@novusai.com>, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-13T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Draft amendment (v1) attached — 16 GPU transition

Ivy — attaching a draft amendment (redwood_amendment_v2.pdf) that:
- updates monthly reserved commit to 16 GPUs 
- adds the 95th pct latency SLO with credit schedule capped at 10% of monthly commit for repeated breaches
- defines 14 business day activation with optional 7-business-day expedite at one-time fee
- outlines proration and Net30 invoicing by default

Please review the SLO language and expedite fee. If this looks good, sign and we’ll kick off activation.

Attachment: redwood_amendment_v2.pdf (Redwood amendment v2 — commercial terms)

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Ivy Chen <ivy@novusai.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-15T10:21:00-07:00
Subject: Ops playbook & fallback details for Novus ramp

Ivy — sharing a focused ops checklist (ops_activation_checklist.xlsx) and a short playbook here: 

- Day 0 (post-signature): HVAC check — hardware allocation request submitted to infra provisioning.
- Day 1–3: Model pin and quantization profile selection in staging; KV cache seeding recommended for hot prefixes.
- Day 4–10: Canary ramp (10% traffic → 50% traffic) against throughput targets; we will enable continuous batching tuned to your latency target.
- Activation complete by Day 14 under standard plan.

Fallback specifics:
- Measurement window: 5-minute rolling, with alerts at 75/90/99 pct capacity.
- Auto-routing: first attempt is pinned quantized variant within your Dedicated pool (no extra cost).
- Burst to hosted: allowed up to 120 aggregate minutes/day across routes (billing at hosted rate).
- If sustained over 24h, our Platform team will open a priority capacity remediation ticket and propose temporary throttles.

I’ll also provide the CLI commands to pre-warm KV caches and an ops playbook excerpt once you confirm the model profile.

Grace O’Connor
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com
From: Ivy Chen <ivy@novusai.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-17T14:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft amendment (v1) attached — 16 GPU transition

Thanks — reviewed with procurement and SRE. A few clarifying points before we sign: 
- Can you change the expedite fee to be a one-time creditable fee if SLOs are missed in the first 60 days? Procurement prefers an incentive-aligned approach.
- We want the burst-to-hosted cap increased to 180 minutes/day for the first 30 days of ramp.
- Please confirm the invoicing effective date aligns to activation completion (we prefer invoice start on activation day rather than signature date).

If you can accept those three edits I’ll route to our CFO for signature today and request DocuSign.

Ivy Chen
VP of Platform, NovusAI
ivy@novusai.com
